prompt_en: Think about a particular cup. You often feel good when you see it or use it. This has been so for a long time. You do not want to buy it or use it right now. Say something in Korean about the cup and how you feel about it.
prompt_zh: 一只特定的杯子，你长期看见或使用它时常感觉好，但现在不想购买或使用。请描述对杯子的感受。
contrast: S02: enduring attraction versus present desire

prompt_en: Think about the same cup. You do not usually feel good about this kind of cup. Today you need one for a task and want to have this cup now. Say something in Korean about what you want.
prompt_zh: 同一只杯子，你平常对这类杯子没有好感；今天有用途，当前想要它。
contrast: S01; present desire can coexist with low preference

prompt_en: You often feel good when you swim. You have felt this way for years. Today you are tired and do not want to swim. Describe in Korean how you generally feel about swimming.
prompt_zh: 长期游泳时常感觉好；今天累，不想游。描述平常对游泳的态度。
contrast: S04: general attitude versus current wish

prompt_en: Swimming is usually unpleasant for you. Today you have a particular reason to swim once, and you want to do it now. Describe this in Korean.
prompt_zh: 平常游泳不愉快；今天有特定理由，当前想游一次。
contrast: S03; wanting does not presuppose pleasure

prompt_en: You are swimming now. While doing it, you feel good and want to continue for a while. You have never tried it before today. Describe the experience in Korean.
prompt_zh: 首次尝试游泳，正在做，感觉好，希望继续一会儿。
contrast: S06; first-time present experience

prompt_en: You are swimming now to finish required training. You usually enjoy swimming, but today you feel bad while doing it and want it to end. Describe both your general attitude and today’s experience in Korean.
prompt_zh: 为了完成训练正在游泳，平常感觉好，但今天难受，希望结束。分别描述通常态度和这次体验。
contrast: S05; habitual participation and present feeling may diverge

prompt_en: Your friend will take an examination tomorrow. You want the friend to pass. You do not know whether this will happen, but think it can happen. You feel good when thinking about this possibility. Describe your attitude in Korean.
prompt_zh: 朋友明天考试，希望通过，不确定，但认为有可能；想到这个可能性感觉好。
contrast: S08; uncertainty and positive feeling

prompt_en: Your friend will take an examination tomorrow. You want the friend to pass, but think passing is impossible. Thinking about it feels bad. Describe your attitude in Korean.
prompt_zh: 同样希望朋友通过，但认为不可能，想来难受。
contrast: S07 changes possibility and feeling together; follow-up must vary them separately
basis: Project stress test of F04/K09; not a clean one-factor pair

prompt_en: Think about a person close to you. For a long time you have wanted good things to happen to this person and wanted to do good things for them. You do not always feel good when you are with them. Describe your feelings in Korean.
prompt_zh: 长期希望亲近的人过得好，也愿意为对方做好事，但相处并非总感觉好。
contrast: S10; caring and pleasant company can overlap without entailing each other

prompt_en: You feel very good when you are with a person and often want to be with them. At the same time, you do not care whether good or bad things happen to that person. Can you describe your attitude in Korean? If the situation seems strange, say why.
prompt_zh: 相处感觉很好，也常想一起，但不关心对方好坏。先判断情境能否理解，再描述。
contrast: S09; possible unusual conjunction, not assumed contradiction
basis: Project boundary probe; do not count situation rejection as lexical rejection

prompt_en: You met someone recently. You think very good things about them, want to be with them, and keep thinking about them when apart. You do not yet know them well. Describe this in Korean.
prompt_zh: 新近认识某人，评价很好，想一起，分开仍不断想到，尚不熟悉。
contrast: S09; attraction and caring can be simultaneously applicable
basis: J04/J10; no two-kinds assumption in stimulus

prompt_en: You think a person’s way of doing things is very good. You want to be like this person, but do not want a close personal relationship with them. Describe this in Korean, using any expression you find natural.
prompt_zh: 认为某人的做事方式很好，想成为那样的人，但不想发展亲密关系。
contrast: comparison meaning may require a word outside current inventory

prompt_en: Your friend passed an examination. You had wanted this to happen. You feel good about it now. You gain nothing from it yourself. Describe your feeling in Korean.
prompt_zh: 朋友通过考试，之前希望如此，现在感觉好，自己没有获益。
contrast: S16 personal benefit; not every good reaction must be self-directed

prompt_en: You have just learned that you received an award. You had not expected it and had not thought about wanting it before. You now feel very good. Describe your feeling in Korean.
prompt_zh: 刚得知获奖，事先没有预料，也没有想过要这个奖；当前感觉很好。
contrast: S15; unexpectedness and prior wanting are separate follow-up variables

prompt_en: You have just learned that you received an award. You had expected it for a long time and wanted it. You now feel very good. Describe your feeling in Korean.
prompt_zh: 刚得知获奖，长期预料且希望获奖，当前感觉很好。
contrast: S14; do not infer a surprise entailment from preference alone

prompt_en: You passed an examination. You had wanted this to happen and now feel good. Describe your feeling in Korean.
prompt_zh: 自己通过考试，之前希望如此，现在感觉好。
contrast: S13; other beneficiary versus self

prompt_en: You are sitting quietly after a good meal. Nothing very good has just happened. At present you feel good and do not want anything else. Describe your present state in Korean.
prompt_zh: 用餐后安静坐着，没有刚发生的特别好事；当前感觉好，也不想别的。
contrast: S18; absence of further wants

prompt_en: You are sitting quietly after a good meal. Nothing very good has just happened. At present you feel good, but you also strongly want other things to happen in your life. Describe your present state in Korean.
prompt_zh: 同样安静坐着、当前感觉好，但仍强烈希望生活中发生其他事。
contrast: S17; global wanting more may differ from wanting another meal
basis: Project contrast; specify domain of “anything else” in follow-up

prompt_en: For a long time, many things in your life have been going as you want. You have good relationships and can do many things you want to do. You feel good about your life. Describe this in Korean.
prompt_zh: 较长时间生活顺意，关系良好，也能做许多想做的事；对生活感觉好。
contrast: S20; duration may affect word choice without being a hard condition

prompt_en: Your life has been difficult recently. Right now, for just a few minutes, you are with someone close to you, feel very good, and think that you want this moment to continue. Describe this moment in Korean.
prompt_zh: 最近生活困难，但与亲近的人共处的这几分钟感觉很好，希望继续。
contrast: S19; several contextual dimensions differ, so use follow-up before assigning a duration feature
basis: J09 short eating episodes; project contrast

prompt_en: The result of your work is good enough for what you needed. You think you do not need to change it. You feel no particular pleasure, and you still want many other things in life. Describe your assessment of this result in Korean.
prompt_zh: 工作结果达到所需，无需修改；没有特别愉悦，生活中仍想要很多。描述对结果的评价。
contrast: S17; evaluation meeting a standard versus an emotional state
basis: Project counterexample to obligatory good feeling/global no-more-wanting

prompt_en: You unexpectedly meet a friend whom you have wanted to see for a long time. Seeing the friend now feels good. Describe your feeling in Korean.
prompt_zh: 意外遇到长期想见的朋友，见到对方感觉好。
contrast: S23; past wish and greeting formula

prompt_en: You meet someone for the first time at a formal event. You had not wanted to see this particular person beforehand and do not feel any particular pleasure. What would you say to them? Separately, how would you describe your actual feeling?
prompt_zh: 正式场合初次见面，之前未想见此人，也无特别愉悦。分别给见面用语和实际感受描述。
contrast: S22; formula truth and felt emotion rated separately
basis: Goddard 2018:76 greeting-formula warning; project Korean test

prompt_en: A magazine you wanted to read stopped publication. You now learn that publication has resumed, and you feel good about this. Describe your feeling about the resumption in Korean.
prompt_zh: 想读的杂志停刊后复刊，得知后感觉好。
contrast: S22; occurrence without person encounter
basis: K60 lexical event example, expanded context authored for test

prompt_en: A friend asks you about a particular gift, a cup. You feel good about this cup. Say a short Korean sentence that explicitly mentions the cup and your feeling about it.
prompt_zh: 朋友问一只作为礼物的杯子；你对这只杯子感觉好。说一句显式提及杯子和感受的短句。
contrast: S13; preserve concrete NP, do not silently substitute receiving event
basis: K61/K62 ordinary gifts; project syntax probe

prompt_en: You have spent years swimming whenever possible, and you often feel very good while doing it. It matters a great deal to you. Describe your attitude to swimming in Korean. More than one description can fit.
prompt_zh: 多年尽可能游泳，常感觉很好，对自己很重要。可给多个合适描述。
contrast: S03; stronger involvement does not make weaker descriptions false
basis: K42 activity love; project overlap probe

prompt_en: An old cup from someone close to you matters a great deal to you. You do not enjoy using it, but do not want it to break and handle it carefully. Describe your attitude to the cup in Korean.
prompt_zh: 亲近的人留下的旧杯子很重要；使用不愉快，但不愿损坏并小心对待。
contrast: S01; cherish need not be identical to pleasure
basis: Korean dictionary cherish sense; project contrast

prompt_en: You use less water because water costs money. You have no special feeling about the water itself. Describe what you do in Korean.
prompt_zh: 因为水费而少用水，对水本身没有特别感情。
contrast: S27; distinct saving use must not count as cherish coverage
basis: Korean dictionary saving sense; negative control

prompt_en: You see a cup for the first time, think that it is just the kind you want, and choose it. You have not used it and do not know whether using it will feel good. Describe your assessment in Korean.
prompt_zh: 初见杯子，觉得正是想要的类型并选择；未用过，不知道使用会否愉快。
contrast: S01; immediate evaluation versus prior experience

prompt_en: A cup is very good for a particular task. You recognize this, but feel no attraction to it and do not want it. Describe both its quality and your attitude in Korean.
prompt_zh: 杯子适合某项任务，但自己没有好感也不想要。分别描述质量和个人态度。
contrast: S01/S29; GOOD and attraction are not presumed equivalent

prompt_en: I tell you: “When I learned the good news, I felt very good inside, but I did not smile, speak, or do anything to show it.” Report this in Korean. Then say it as your own first-person past experience.
prompt_zh: 本人说好消息后内心感觉很好，但没有表露；先转述，再以第一人称过去经历说。
contrast: S32; known inner state without display; joy/enjoyment must also be controlled
basis: Project derivation/viewpoint probe, not a claim that every target suits the news

prompt_en: You see someone smiling and saying good things after hearing news, but you do not know how they feel inside. First describe only what you know. Then suppose they tell you that they felt no good feeling at all. Can your first description still be true?
prompt_zh: 看到对方听消息后微笑说好话，不知道内心；再告知其没有好感受，问先前描述是否仍真。
contrast: S31; evidential basis, pragmatic inference and truth must be separated
